title: Nor do they mean the act can fail to follow upon efficacious grace and a settled judgment
source_text: XXV. Ac praeterea quum dicunt agens liberum, positis omnibus ad agendum praerequisitis, posse agere vel non agere, hoc, aut illud agere, mens eorum non est quod positis omnibus quae ad aliquem actum voluntatis praerequiruntur, inter quae locum habet gratiae divinae motio, & practicae mentis judicium, possit actio voluntatis non sequi, & sic carentia actionis ejus jungi cum omnibus illis per quae voluntas ad agendum movetur atque disponitur. Fatentur enim impossibile esse ut Deus hominem quempiam gratia sua efficaci ad aliquem actum pietatis moveat, & tamen actus ille ab eo non eliciatur: aut ut aliquis, omnibus expensis, judicet hic & nunc istud sibi agendum & appetendum esse, & tamen idem istud non agat & appetat; Verum id solum sibi volunt illum qui, qua jam dictum est ratione, ad agendum movetur, licet infallibiliter & certo acturus sit, & contingere non possit ut non agat; illum, inquam, nihilominus veram in se retinere potentiam non agendi, & aliter agendi, quae manet non solum in eo qui proxime ad agendum paratus & dispositus est, sed in eo ipso qui jam de facto agit; quoniam etsi cum actu aliquo stare non possit ejus carentia, aut actus contrarius, optime tamen cum eo componi potest potentia ad actum illum contrarium, ut jam pluries inculcatum fuit.
pass_a_gloss: And moreover when they say that a free agent, all things prerequisite to acting being posited, can act or not act, do this, or that, their mind is not that, all things being posited which are prerequired to some act of the will, among which the motion of divine grace has place, and the judgment of the practical mind, the action of the will can fail to follow, and thus the lack of its action be joined with all those things by which the will is moved and disposed to acting. For they confess it impossible that God should move any man by his efficacious grace to some act of piety, and yet that act not be elicited by him: or that someone, all things weighed, should judge that this must be done and desired by him here and now, and yet the same not do and desire it; But they mean only this, that he who, in the manner already stated, is moved to acting, although he will infallibly and certainly act, and it cannot happen that he not act; he, I say, nevertheless retains in himself a true potency of not acting, and of acting otherwise, which remains not only in him who is proximately prepared and disposed to act, but in him himself who already in fact acts; since although with some act its lack, or a contrary act, cannot stand, yet with it the potency to that contrary act can very well be composed, as has already been inculcated many times.
pass_b_english: Further, when they say that a free agent, given everything required beforehand for acting, can act or not act, and do this or that, they do not mean that the will's act can fail to follow once everything required for some act of will is in place, including the motion of God's grace and the practical judgment of the mind, so that the absence of the act could coexist with everything that moves and disposes the will to act.

They admit it is impossible for God to move someone by his effective grace to an act of godliness and for that act not to be produced, or for someone, having weighed everything, to judge that he must do and seek something here and now and then not do and seek it.

All they mean is this. The man who is moved to act in the way described will act infallibly and surely, and it cannot happen that he does not act; yet he still keeps in himself a real power not to act and to act otherwise. That power remains not only in someone fully prepared and ready to act but in someone actually acting. For although an act cannot coexist with its own absence or with a contrary act, the power to the contrary act can perfectly well coexist with it, as has been stressed many times already.

choices.why: Kept as the Schools' technical term; Le Blanc fixes its sense as a real power to act otherwise, not a state of balance between options.
